issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: The template's example usage (Main.java) and the problem description imply Animal subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) should be constructible with a single String name argument, but the solution implementation requires two parameters (String name, int age) in the constructors of Animal and all subclasses. This difference will confuse students following the template/example and cause compilation errors if they implement single-argument constructors as implied by the problem/template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Either (A) remove the extra age parameter from Animal and all subclass constructors in the solution (change constructors to accept only String name) so they match the UML/problem/template examples, or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and the template Main.java examples to document and use the additional int age parameter so all artifacts expect (String name, int age).

issues.description: Attribute mismatch in Animal: The UML and problem description state that Animal has a name attribute (and students are instructed that animals share a name), but the solution's Animal class introduces an additional 'age' attribute that is not described in the problem/UML. This discrepancy changes the required class state and is the likely cause of the constructor mismatch above, creating confusion about which attributes students must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the set of attributes for Animal across artifacts. Either remove the 'age' field from the solution's Animal class (and related constructor parameters and getters/setters) so Animal only contains 'name' as per the UML/problem, or update the problem statement and UML to explicitly include 'age' as an Animal attribute and update template examples accordingly.
